first.rationale: Activation and onboarding completion are both down this quarter, and inherited memory (memory_31, memory_86) shows onboarding simplification produces durable activation gains for SMB/self-serve accounts—directly addressing the observed metric declines without the known retention harm. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given competitor pressure, but that memory explicitly warns against generalizing it due to material 30-day retention damage, which conflicts with the objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue; I verified it to confirm the warning still holds before ruling it out. I also verified memory_31 to confirm the onboarding-simplification result is robust before committing scarce experiment capacity to it. Running this as a small guarded test rather than a broad rollout preserves ability to catch any unexpected downstream effects (e.g., on lead quality or later-stage retention) before scaling.
